quote: Anything can happen.
author: Mark Douglas, Trading in the Zone
note: The first of Douglas's five fundamental truths. Every trade and every investment has an uncertain outcome. Accept that before you enter, not after.

quote: Cut your losses short and let your profits run.
author: Classic trading maxim
note: Most investors do the opposite: they sell winners quickly to feel good and hold losers hoping to break even. Reverse the habit and the maths starts working for you.

quote: The consistency you seek is in your mind, not in the markets.
author: Mark Douglas
note: Markets will never become predictable. What can become consistent is your process: your rules, your sizing and your reactions.

quote: You have power over how you'll respond to uncertainty.
author: Yvan Byeajee (@TradingComposur)
book: The Essence of Trading Psychology in One Skill
note: You can't control the next tick. You can control your reaction to it, and that's where consistency is built.

quote: Buy high, sell higher.
author: Momentum maxim
note: Strength tends to persist. Momentum investing buys what is already rising and holds while the trend lasts, which is the opposite of our instinct to 'buy cheap'.

quote: It never was my thinking that made the big money for me. It always was my sitting.
author: Jesse Livermore, Reminiscences of a Stock Operator
note: Being right is only half the job. The fortune is made by having the patience to stay with a winning position.

quote: You don't need to know what is going to happen next in order to make money.
author: Mark Douglas
note: An edge plays out over many trades, not one. Stop trying to predict the next move and start trusting a tested process.

quote: Freedom from blind reactivity begins with self-awareness.
author: Yvan Byeajee (@TradingComposur)
book: The Essence of Trading Psychology in One Skill
note: Notice the urge before you act on it. That pause is where most bad trades are avoided.

quote: The elements of good trading are: cutting losses, cutting losses, and cutting losses.
author: Ed Seykota, Market Wizards
note: Survival comes first. A small loss is a cost of doing business; a big loss is what ends careers and wrecks portfolios.

quote: Be fearful when others are greedy and greedy when others are fearful.
author: Warren Buffett
note: Crowd emotion creates mispricing. The hardest and most rewarding moments to invest are when everyone around you is scared.

quote: Every moment in the market is unique.
author: Mark Douglas
note: Today's setup may look like last month's, but it is never identical. Treat each trade on its own merits and drop the baggage of the last one.

quote: Confidence is not "I will profit on this trade." Confidence is "I will be fine if I don't profit from this trade."
author: Yvan Byeajee (@TradingComposur)
book: The Essence of Trading Psychology in One Skill
note: Real confidence comes from accepting the risk in advance, not from being sure of the outcome.

quote: Losers average losers.
author: Paul Tudor Jones
note: Adding to a losing trade to 'lower your average' is how small mistakes become big ones. In trading, add to strength, not to weakness.

quote: The trend is your friend, until the end when it bends.
author: Trading maxim
note: Trading with the trend tilts the odds your way. Respecting your exit rule protects you when the trend finally turns.

quote: When you genuinely accept the risks, you will be at peace with any outcome.
author: Mark Douglas
note: Fear comes from trades where the risk was never really accepted. Define the loss before you enter, and the outcome stops controlling your emotions.

quote: Money matters, but not as much as you probably think.
author: Yvan Byeajee (@TradingComposur)
book: The Essence of Trading Psychology in One Skill
note: Fixating on money tightens your decisions. Focusing on process frees them.

quote: Rule No. 1: Never lose money. Rule No. 2: Never forget rule No. 1.
author: Warren Buffett
note: Not literally avoiding every loss, but respecting downside first. A 50% loss needs a 100% gain just to get back to where you started.

quote: The market is never wrong; opinions often are.
author: Jesse Livermore (attributed)
note: Arguing with price is expensive. When the market disagrees with your view, the market is the one paying out.

quote: An edge is nothing more than an indication of a higher probability of one thing happening over another.
author: Mark Douglas
note: An edge is a probability, not a certainty. Losing trades are part of every winning system, and that is fine.

quote: In order to succeed, you first have to be willing to experience failure.
author: Yvan Byeajee (@TradingComposur)
book: The Essence of Trading Psychology in One Skill
note: Losing trades are part of every winning system. Accept them as the cost of doing business.

quote: The big money is not in the buying and selling, but in the waiting.
author: Charlie Munger
note: Activity feels productive, but long-term wealth comes from letting good investments compound undisturbed.

quote: The investor's chief problem, and even his worst enemy, is likely to be himself.
author: Benjamin Graham
note: Markets don't ruin most investors. Fear, greed and impatience do. Know your own behaviour as well as you know your portfolio.

quote: There is a random distribution between wins and losses for any given set of variables that define an edge.
author: Mark Douglas
note: Ten trades with a 60% edge can still start with five losses in a row. Judge a system over many trades, never over the last few.

quote: Trading doesn't just reveal your character, it also builds it if you stay in the game long enough.
author: Yvan Byeajee (@TradingComposur)
note: Markets expose impatience, ego and fear, and give you the chance to work on all three.

quote: Win or lose, everybody gets what they want out of the market.
author: Ed Seykota
note: Look honestly at your behaviour. Overtrading may be about excitement; refusing to sell losers may be about avoiding regret. Know what you're really after.

quote: The four most dangerous words in investing are: this time it's different.
author: Sir John Templeton
note: Every bubble comes with a story about why old rules no longer apply. They usually still do.

quote: The hard, cold reality of trading is that every trade has an uncertain outcome.
author: Mark Douglas
note: No analysis removes uncertainty. Position sizing and stop-losses are how you live with it.

quote: Trading effectively is about assessing probabilities, not certainties.
author: Yvan Byeajee (@TradingComposur)
note: No setup is certain. Think in probabilities and size your positions accordingly.

quote: Bull markets are born on pessimism, grow on skepticism, mature on optimism and die on euphoria.
author: Sir John Templeton
note: The mood of the crowd tells you where you are in the cycle. When everyone is euphoric, caution pays.

quote: It's not whether you're right or wrong, but how much you make when you're right and how much you lose when you're wrong.
author: George Soros (attributed)
note: A 40% win rate can be very profitable if winners are much bigger than losers. Focus on the payoff, not on being right.

quote: The market doesn't generate happy or painful information. From the market's perspective, it's all simply information.
author: Mark Douglas
note: Pain comes from how we interpret price moves, not from the moves themselves. Neutral thinking leads to clearer decisions.

quote: The expectation that you bring with you in trading is often the greatest obstacle you will encounter.
author: Yvan Byeajee (@TradingComposur)
note: Expectations turn normal losses into emotional events. Let the outcome be what it is.

quote: Far more money has been lost by investors preparing for corrections than has been lost in corrections themselves.
author: Peter Lynch
note: Sitting in cash waiting for the 'perfect' dip often costs more than simply staying invested through the dip.

quote: If you don't bet, you can't win. If you lose all your chips, you can't bet.
author: Larry Hite, Market Wizards
note: Take risk, but never so much that one bad run knocks you out of the game. Position size is your survival tool.

quote: Know what you own, and know why you own it.
author: Peter Lynch
note: If you can't explain why you hold something in two lines, you won't know what to do when it falls.

quote: All statistics have outliers. Money management, therefore, is key to the process of good trading.
author: Yvan Byeajee (@TradingComposur)
note: Rare events happen more often than we expect. Position sizing is what keeps them survivable.

quote: In the short run, the market is a voting machine, but in the long run it is a weighing machine.
author: Benjamin Graham
note: Sentiment drives prices day to day. Earnings and fundamentals decide where they end up over years.

quote: The first rule of compounding: never interrupt it unnecessarily.
author: Charlie Munger
note: Stopping SIPs, switching funds and early withdrawals all reset the clock that compounding depends on.

quote: The market can stay irrational longer than you can stay solvent.
author: Often attributed to John Maynard Keynes
note: Being right too early can be the same as being wrong. Leverage and stubbornness turn a good idea into a loss.

quote: A quiet mind is able to hear intuition over fear.
author: Yvan Byeajee (@TradingComposur)
note: Calm is a trading edge. Noise, news and emotion drown out good judgement.

quote: Plan your trade and trade your plan.
author: Trading maxim
note: Decide entry, exit and size before the trade, when you're calm. In the heat of the moment, just execute.

quote: Your SIP doesn't know the market fell. That's why it works.
author: HBE Capital
note: Automation removes our worst instinct, reacting to headlines. A SIP keeps buying through fear, collecting more units when prices are low.

quote: Don't focus on making money; focus on protecting what you have.
author: Paul Tudor Jones
note: Defence first. Capital you keep is capital that can compound.

quote: Never let a winning trade go to your head, or a losing trade to your heart.
author: Yvan Byeajee (@TradingComposur)
note: Treat every outcome the same way: as information, not identity.

quote: Volatility is the price of admission, not a penalty.
author: HBE Capital
note: Equity returns come with swings. Investors who treat every dip as a mistake tend to exit right before the recovery that pays for the ride.

quote: A 50% fall needs a 100% gain to recover.
author: The maths of loss
note: This is why risk management matters as much as returns. Avoiding deep drawdowns keeps compounding on track.

quote: Stopping your SIP in a falling market is like walking out of a sale.
author: HBE Capital
note: Lower NAVs mean your fixed amount buys more units. Those cheaper units do the most work when markets recover.

quote: The mind is a fascinating instrument that can make or break you.
author: Yvan Byeajee (@TradingComposur)
note: Your strategy is only as good as the mind executing it.

quote: The best portfolio is the one you can hold in a bad year.
author: HBE Capital
note: A plan you abandon at the first 20% fall is worse than a slightly less 'optimal' plan you actually stick with.

quote: Time in the market beats timing the market.
author: Investing maxim
note: Missing just a handful of the best days can cut long-term returns sharply, and those days often arrive in the scariest periods.

quote: The plan is written in calm. It's tested in panic.
author: HBE Capital
note: Decide now what you'll do if markets fall 10%, 20% or 30%. When it happens, follow the plan instead of the panic.

quote: Patience is a position.
author: HBE Capital
note: Holding through uncertainty is an active choice that takes discipline. Long-term investors are paid for exactly that.
